title: Function Hotspot Profile
body:
Overview

This record documents Function Hotspot Profile within the Performance Profiling and Optimization Database. Stores benchmarks and measured optimization results. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record is measurement before change: run a defined workload, record timings and resource use, change exactly one thing, and measure again under the same workload. Results are reported as measured numbers on defined inputs, never as general claims. An optimization is kept only when the re-measurement confirms it and correctness checks still pass.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: samples: 10. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

An engineer uses these records to spend effort where it pays: the profile names the hotspot, the benchmark proves the gain, and the record preserves both so the next reader does not re-litigate the same trade-off. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Function Hotspot Profile: summarize benchmark timings and the gain from one change.
before = [121, 138, 155, 172, 189, 206, 133, 150, 167, 184]
after = [round(x * 0.72, 1) for x in before]
def median(xs):
    s = sorted(xs)
    return (s[len(s) // 2 - 1] + s[len(s) // 2]) / 2 if len(s) % 2 == 0 else s[len(s) // 2]
def p95(xs):
    s = sorted(xs)
    return s[int(0.95 * (len(s) - 1))]
print("samples:", len(before))
print("before median ms:", median(before), "p95 ms:", p95(before), "max ms:", max(before))
print("after median ms:", median(after), "p95 ms:", p95(after), "max ms:", max(after))
print("median reduction ms:", round(median(before) - median(after), 1))
demo_output:
samples: 10
before median ms: 161.0 p95 ms: 189 max ms: 206
after median ms: 115.9 p95 ms: 136.1 max ms: 148.3
median reduction ms: 45.1
